## IO Vapoura \[Variations\] \[[Free DL](https://sanjayaprime.bandcamp.com/album/io-vapoura-variations)\]

**San Jaya Prime**

**Original Release Date**: 2010, July 7

When I released the 20-Year Anniversary Edition of "[IO Limiters](io-limiters)", the question I heard most was, "Are we getting IO Vapoura?" Yes, yes you are. It's my favorite album, it's the fan favorite from the IO series, and I'm going all out for it. In fact, you're getting two, as there will be a sunrise side with lighter versions of each song, then a sunset side with darker versions. Just like the original, every song has its own art, inspired by those same pieces (some of which now appear in video game art and magazines). Yes, that's two new pieces of art for each side to each song. Also, some of the lost tracks from the Unversioned cut of the album will be making an appearance, including fan favorite "More than Human" among others. Look for that in 2030.

**Bonus**: If you want to see one of the new pieces of art for my award-winning song "Synapse Collapse", then it's included as the final frame of the music video that we put together for my collaboration with Alchemorph Soundtracks, KeOSz, and Mtwn -- _"A Drill About Childhood in Persia"_ ([YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UdUc1AkdLDY)).

### But what about the story?

Long-time fans will remember the overarching story of IO. In Vapoura, a single scientist is sent into the ODN server. Humanity has been granted a space inside it to run a simulation using a portion of its processing power. IO Vapoura explores the boons alongside the risks of such a treaty, closing out the story shortly after a visit to the Bazaar of Wonders and a final goodbye at a tea house... under paper shadows. The original story was lost with our website more than a decade ago. I even checked The Wayback Machine, but it was never catalogued. It's all still in my head, so this time around I'm putting it in book form. That will also be released along with the new cut of the album in 2030.

texts: "To say I enjoy this album would be an understatement."

content.text:
## Vapoura: The Cover Art

This is one of five production-level pieces of artwork that I used Blender for. I could see it perfectly in my mind, and while my perspective sketches of the cover turned out pretty good, it needed to be crisp, clear, 'n crystalline! If "[IO Limiters](io-limiters)" was the water element of the series, then "IO Vapoura" was air. To me, crystals are connected to air, and therefore needed to be in the music and the art... ethereal tinkling always off in the distance. The art also needed to represent a virtual simulation, housing a space running many other simulated experiences inside of it. I combined it with NASA's imagery of The Pleiades along with my signature fractal, all of which surrounds and forms the warp gate that Vapoura is emerging from.

## Vapoura: The Music

1.  **Gongo Dodan**: Translated literally from the Japanese as "words fail", and while the common idiom has grown to translate to "inexcusable", the original Zen is an expression of awe that cannot be spoken of -- _ineffable_. That is why the art for this track is an empty canvas. The song itself uses a gong transition between each fourth, something that my drummer BMFD has smiled about, saying, "Here comes the gong transition!" And he's right, I love it! It remains to this day one of my most remixed tracks, both by myself and by others.
2.  **Non-finite**: When I got back the recorded lyrics from SPEQTRA, I was like, "Well shit... how do I make a song that lives up to these lyrics?" She went all in, and the original ethereal version I was working on ended up needing months of rework, because there was no way we were re-recording her vox when she'd rocked it so hard the first time around. _The sky is the limit!_
3.  **Le Miracle de la Machine**: There were some months in there where LiLi Glitch had this as her wake-up alarm. Not me. I won't and can't wake up to so smooth a song. I need blaring alarms and usually three of them if I'm going to wake up. _"La vérité fini toujours par se découvrir."_ My original piano progression was more jazz-like, then I 180d on this, going instead with the more smooth crescendo that connects the first half of the song to the second, passing from one to the next... as a parent to a child.
4.  **Halcyon Electronica**: I still don't know if I'll be including this on the 20-year anniversary cut. I've grown farther and farther away from 4x4s like this. The OG song could have easily fit on "CD2 - Tears of Ra" -- which, despite the title, was my first ever DJ mix. In fact, yes, thinking back to the original vision, I definitely have more to say thru a 4x4 medium. It's happening.
5.  **At a tea house, under paper shadows**: One of the more "Eastern" influenced songs on the album, especially in part in thanks to Jade. Watching the difference between playing cello and playing a mandolin gave me an idea of the physics, the sounds themselves, and that grew into how to emulate them. By this point in the album, you can hear the underlying melody that each song is a variation of. I'll be scrapping that adherence in the 20-year edition, although you'll certainly be hearing new versions of "Paper Shadows" coming your way.
6.  **A day in the Bazaar of Wonders**: The crowd favorite on the album. Easily. I was inspired by Khaled's "Alech Taadi" ([YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wNAwYdmBB0Y)) on the OST for "The Fifth Element" and wanted to combine it with the beat from "Aknot! Wot?" (same OST). Sampling from the Bollywood public domain, I put together the beat under the classic snake-charmer flute, finishing it out with my own guitar riff. I got messages sent my way about it showing up in some series called "Fuller House", as well as "Deli Boys", but that's not my song; that's "Boom Boom" by Photronique ([YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JnARVNmAWOE&list=RDJnARVNmAWOE&start_radio=1&pp=ygUZQm9vbSBCb29tIGJ5IFBob3Ryb25pcXVlCqAHAdIHCQmZCwGHKiGM7w%3D%3D)). We sampled from the same classic, as did Timmy Trumpet 'n Dimatik for their song "Punjabi" ([YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0FRlJkUSKv8)). I can say I was first to use the sample by at least five years, but Photronique has better marketing compared to my non-existent licensing department.
7.  **LAW (The Threefold Goddess)**: Returning to a bit of the brokenbeat vibe of "IO Limiters", but more airy and in some ways more intimate. The law of land, sea, and air; past, present, and future. What goes up, must come down... at least when in the domain of law on a planet, where gravity is the ultimate judge. What goes up in space? Well that keeps going up, unless it falls under a different domain of law. Understanding who holds enforcement over the laws you live by gives you the key to the domain.
8.  **IO Vapoura**: Long-time fans will recognize my signature synth sequence here, where I signed the title track itself. However, I have to say... I tried to put too much in the same track. If I do include this on the anniversary edition, it will have quite a few differences. In some ways it was my first experiment in psybient textures, which has since grown far out of these initial simple origins.
9.  **1 love 0 \[infinitely\]**: My friend Sharif, the one person I can say has out-hitch-hiked me in terms of travel across this planet, still to this day signs his messages with "infinitely". For more commentary on the title, read "[All That Is](all-that-is)". Since I've decided to include a new version of "Halcyon Electronica" on the anniversary edition, that one will go on the sunset side of the album while this one will go on the sunrise section. I'll be bringing in more Eastern additions for that remake.
10.  **To Summon the Sky**: Secretly, the "Gears of Heaven" has already been remixed in a way. Playing around with the flute section as brought out some of our best live songs, some of which made it into the New Mexico portion of "[Into the Southwest](into-the-southwest)". Also, it's the spiritual successor to crowd favorite "The Witching Wall" ([on "IO Pulse" here on Bandcamp](https://sanjayaprime.bandcamp.com/album/io-pulse)). I'm hoping that with the anniversary edition, I can finally bring all of these together. I've already started testing it out and I'm excited to breathe new life into the gears.
11.  **Synapse Collapse**: Another fan favorite and, in fact, was once runner-up in the 2999 competition put on by Peppermill Records (later on King Deluxe). While my song "Escape from Hunahpu" won out and took top five in that competition, I wasn't done with "Synapse Collapse". I scrapped the original "Lovers' Quarrel" cut of the song, exploring even more of the noise side. By the way, to my fans of noise and glitch who love this side of my music, so much love to you! Seriously! In the version I released on the album, I knew exactly what I wanted to title it. But for that story, you need to know about Atomjack ([fUSION Anomaly](https://fusionanomaly.net/atomjack.html)). I remember the Mosaic browser and the time when the internet was just text. Then came Netscape Navigator, and with it came images, even moving images like GIFs. If you weren't there, you don't get how magical it was. Then in late '99, early 2k, came a little site called fUSION Anomaly... years before Wikipedia. The nodes of the site linked together, making connections between otherwise disparate concepts. Talking with Atomjack, this early form of connection made a mark on me, to the point that to this very day fusion and hybrids are what really holds my interest, no matter whether in food, music, design, or otherwise. When I reached out to Atomjack about naming this mix after the site, he said yes, adding simply, "I'm honored." The anomaly lives on to this very day ([Main Site](https://fusionanomaly.net/)) ([OG on Wayback Machine](https://web.archive.org/web/20001119220400/http://www.fusionanomaly.net/)).
12.  **May Angels Take You**: Whereas we open almost every live show with "Gongo Dodan" in some form or another, our penultimate track since 2011 has been the "Dying Vicariously" mix of "May Angels Take You". The original version has one of the more incredible crescendos among all my works, evolving through three distinct phases, and pulling from Arabic folklore along the way before going into the final explosive section of the song's audio triptych.
13.  **Last Train to Sheol**: The stories of "the ghost train" have taken many forms over the past few thousand years, everything as far back as "the caravan of the night" that trails into the Sahara carrying the dead. It is the ethereal, crystalline finale of the original album. In many ways, I already completed what I came to do with this song. That means it's unlikely to see a recursion on any future edition. You can feel the train moving around you, the landscape passing by, and the ever-present sense of approaching the light while darkness gathers all around you. Mission accomplished. Game over.

content.text: ## IO Vapoura \[Unversioned & Unfinished\] With the original being such a big hit, I started working on some of the songs again... along with some that were never finished. Once the "IO" series came to a close with "The Last Memory of Laughter" in 2012, January, that freed me to work on these newer versions. I'd scrapped the idea of following variations, as with the original "IO Vapoura", which let me go back and explore paths that I'd previously abandoned... leaving them behind just to hold true to that core harmony behind the originals. But by the end of 2014, the tumor that knocked out my hearing when I was six-years old had finally done enough damage to bring down my other ear. Others were letting me know about things that sounded "off" in my music, and worse, I myself could _not_ hear those things. It was over. I released the last unversioned, non-variation, and unfinished songs that I'd been working on for "IO Vapoura" in the video above. With that, I retired from production music, focusing on playing live shows along with DJ sets... and pushing my design work to the forefront of my public face. My fractal and graphic design arts had taken second place for nearly a decade. It was time to put on a different face. It's been more than a decade since that moment. My hearing hasn't magically improved. If anything, it's gotten worse. What _has_ improved is the technology itself. A mastering bus now comes standard for nearly every MPC, even Koala Sampler on my iPad, letting me run samples through it and master right at the source-audio level. On top of that, I've abandoned quite a bit of the glitch elements that was once part of my signature sound. I can't trust my hearing to work with it. Then finally, to wrap off each song I run it through a combo of a simple limiter with a follow-up compressor pass and in Audacity, where my final levels that I can see with my eyes _should_ be showing what others would be hearing. I hope. My tribe and inner circle hasn't told me anything different. If anything, the response to my newer music has been excellent! So yes, we're returning together to the floating virtual city of Halcyon inside the electronic simulation of Vapoura. It's going to take a few years to get it all put together, but it's happening. 2030 is just around the corner. ## IO Vapoura (20-Year Anniversary Edition) _Coming 2030, July_ Look for the complete two-disc "Sunset" and "Sunrise" anniversary edition of _IO Vapoura_ in 2030. At that point, most of this page will go into a "Bonus Page" of easter eggs leading up to that edition. That should also include a part of the writings and more from the _IO_ extended universe.

texts:
## Extended Listening

If you like even a little of what you've heard with "IO Vapoura", then you can hear one of our live versions of "Gongo Dodan" and "May Angels Take You" on our set of lives songs, "[Warriors in Waiting](warriors-in-waiting-live-set)" (2005 - 2018). Vapoura, as the air element, naturally connects with "[IO Limiters](io-limiters)", the water element, to form the spirit of the moon. They form a natural bond in both listening and visuals. Then many fans of Vapoura have also loved my "[Last Memory of Fire](last-memory-of-fire)" remix that pays tribute to the _Alien_ franchise. Then for the art surrounding the series, you would definitely like a few of [my surreal fractalscapes](#?/other-fractalscapes).
